title: topic_output_schema
description: Canonical output schema for Agent 5 (Writer). Every topic generated by the Writer must conform to this schema exactly. The orchestrator validates against this before writing to Supabase.

topic_name.description: Exact topic name as it appears in the syllabus.

priority.description: Derived from Topic DNA. high = 2+ PYQ appearances or recent 6-mark topic. medium = 1 appearance, 3–6 marks. low = 1 appearance, 2 marks. never_asked = on syllabus, zero PYQ appearances.

difficulty.description: Relative difficulty for this paper's student cohort.

estimated_study_minutes.description: Calibrated to priority and content depth. never_asked: 5. 2-mark: 15. 3-4 mark: 25. 6-mark: 45–60.

depth_signal_source.description: What governed depth decisions for this topic.

rapid_revision.description: Written last, placed first. Minimum viable exam knowledge. A student reading only this must answer a 2-mark DU question.

definition_one_line.description: Under 15 words. DU-acceptable for full marks on a 2-mark define question. No LaTeX unless essential.

key_formula_or_concept.description: Single most tested LaTeX expression or concept sentence. For theory topics: the single most important statement.

examiner_pattern.description: Exact instruction word DU uses + typical question phrasing from Language DNA. For Tier 3: 'No NEP exam data available for this topic.'

definition.description: Under 40 words. No undefined terms beyond the prerequisite bridge. DU-acceptable for 2-mark answer. All math in LaTeX.

core_concept.description: Plain language explanation. No assumed knowledge beyond prerequisite. Written for exam use. May include analogy inline.

analogy.description: Verified analogy connecting to the prerequisite bridge. Factually correct — not merely evocative.

analogy_verified.description: true only if the analogy is a factually accurate comparison. false or null if analogy is metaphorical or unverified.

examples.description: Worked examples. For numerical papers: full step-by-step with LaTeX, units on every intermediate, answer boxed. For theory: DU-use-case examples.

content.description: The problem statement or example setup.

steps.description: Ordered solution steps. For theory examples: may be empty [].

step_text.description: Full step in LaTeX where any math appears. Units shown on intermediate values.

units_shown.description: true if this step shows units on numeric values. null for symbolic steps.

answer.description: Final answer. For numerical: LaTeX display math in \boxed{}.

answer_boxed.description: true for all numerical examples — mandatory. null for theory examples.

common_error.description: Specific error that loses marks in DU for this exact problem type. Not generic advice.

verified.description: Set false on Writer output. Agent 7 sets true after verification passes.

verification_mode.description: numerical_dual for high-priority numericals. numerical_single for medium/low. proof for proof topics. none for theory.

verification_passed.description: null on Writer output. Agent 7 sets true/false.

diagram_block.description: Diagram block for diagram-heavy papers or 6-mark topics requiring a diagram. null for non-diagram topics.

svg_source.description: library for complex biological structures. generated for simple geometric/flow diagrams.

svg_file_path.description: Library path for svg_source=library. null for generated.

svg_code.description: Minimal renderable SVG code for svg_source=generated. null for library.

explanation.description: One-line explanation of this part's function.

du_expected_label.description: Exact label DU expects in exam diagrams — sourced from textbook.

marks_value.description: Approximate marks this diagram carries in DU exams.

draw_instructions.description: Step-by-step guide for drawing this diagram in an exam.

examiners_note.description: Exact instruction word DU uses. Specific PYQ year reference (Tier 1/2). What full marks includes that passing doesn't. Combination pattern if applicable.

examiners_note_pyq_refs.description: PYQ year references cited in examiners_note. e.g. ['2024', '2023'].

instruction_word_frequency.description: Derived from Language DNA. e.g. { 'find': 2, 'prove': 1, 'define': 0 }. null if no Language DNA available.

common_mistakes.description: DU-specific mistakes with marks impact. Not generic study advice.

description.description: Specific mistake students make in DU exams for this topic.

marks_impact.description: How many marks this error costs and why. e.g. 'Loses 2 marks — characteristic equation must appear before eigenvalue calculation.'

answer_writing_technique.description: Present for ALL topics where any PYQ has 6+ marks. null for lower-mark topics.

min_marks_threshold.description: Always 6 — this field only renders for 6-mark questions.

structure.description: Sentence-by-sentence structure of a full-marks answer. Not paragraph-by-paragraph.

marks_distribution.description: Which part of the structure earns which marks. e.g. { 'definition_sentence': 1, 'proof_body': 4, 'conclusion': 1 }

word_count_target.description: For theory: ~150–200 words for a 6-mark answer. For numerical: null (structured steps, not word count).

diagram_expected.description: true if DU expects a diagram in the answer for this question type.

pyqs.description: All PYQs from the normalised collection relevant to this topic. Exact question text — never paraphrased.

year_confirmed.description: true only if confirmed from document content, not just filename.

question_text.description: Exact verbatim question as it appears in the PYQ. Never paraphrased.

key_steps.description: Specific steps needed to earn full marks. Not generic. Specific to this exact question.

instruction_word.description: Exact instruction word as used in the question: find / prove / define / state / explain / derive / calculate / describe.

recency_weight.description: 1.5 if this is the most recent available PYQ year. 1.0 otherwise.

quick_checks.description: Exactly 3 self-check questions. No answers — ever. Forced active recall. At least one must require application, not just recall.

items.description: A question the student asks themselves. Answerable from the topic content. No trivially easy items.

flagged_fields.description: Set by Writer if it detects its own limitations. e.g. { 'definition': 'syllabus_too_vague', 'examples': 'no_pyq_to_calibrate' }. null if no flags.
